title: Numbers
subtitle: three hundred and sixty-two, per cent, work out
summary: Say big numbers, dates, fractions, decimals and percentages in English, and talk about simple calculations.

lesson.heading: Cardinal numbers
rows: two thousand, eight hundred and sixty
lesson.note: There is no plural -s after hundred, thousand, million and billion when they are part of a number. When we are talking generally, they are plural: thousands of people, millions of insects.

lesson.heading: Dates
lesson.text: With dates, we write them and say them in a different way. We can write 4 June or June 4th, but we say **the fourth of June** or **June the fourth**. Notice that we use an ordinal number (fourth, twenty-first), not a cardinal one.

examples.text: 21 May = **the twenty-first of May** or **May the twenty-first**.
We arrived on **the seventh of April**.
1997 = **nineteen ninety-seven**; 2016 = **two thousand and sixteen** or **twenty sixteen**.

lesson.heading: Fractions and decimals
lesson.note: After the point we say each figure on its own: 6.02 = six point oh two.

lesson.heading: Percentages
lesson.text: 26% is spoken as **twenty-six per cent**. More than 50% of something is the **majority** of it; less than 50% of something is the **minority**.

examples.text: The vast **majority** of the students agreed with the new plan.
About 80% of people were in favour - so the **majority** supported it.

lesson.heading: Calculations
rows: 6 + 4 = 10 (six plus / and four equals / is ten)
6 x 4 = 24 (six multiplied by / times four is twenty-four)

lesson.heading: Working out numbers
lesson.text: When you **work out** an answer, you try to calculate it. If you **add up** numbers, you put them together to reach a total. If you **get stuck**, you have a problem and cannot continue. A **calculator** is a small electronic machine for working out numbers.

examples.text: Some people are not very good at **adding up** numbers.
I often **get stuck** if I have to **work out** something quite difficult.
I'm not very good at arithmetic. I always have to use a **calculator**.

lesson.heading: Saying '0'
lesson.text: We say '0' in different ways in different situations. In phone numbers we usually say **oh** or **zero**; in mathematics we say **nought**; with temperature we say **below zero** or **minus**.

examples.text: Phone number 603449 = six **oh** three, **double** four nine.
examples.note: or six zero three, double four nine

examples.text: -10 degrees = ten degrees **below zero**, or **minus** ten degrees.

lesson.text: Never add -s to hundred, thousand or million inside a number: the crowd was over twenty thousand, not ~~twenty thousands~~.

options: two thousand, three hundred and forty-five
two thousands, three hundred and forty-five
two thousand, three hundreds and forty-five
two thousand and three hundred forty-five
exercises.explanation: No plural -s inside a number, and we put and before the last part.

exercises.prompt: In mathematics, 0.25 is spoken as ___ point two five.
exercises.explanation: In mathematics we say nought for '0'.
We say the number + per cent.

exercises.statement: Eight divided by two is four.
exercises.explanation: Correct. 8 / 2 = 4, and we say 'eight divided by two is four'.

exercises.statement: After the game, I heard that the crowd was over twenty thousands.
exercises.explanation: After the game, I heard that the crowd was over twenty thousand. There is no plural -s after thousand in a number.

exercises.prompt: How do you say the date 10 September?
exercises.explanation: We say the + ordinal number + of + month (or September the tenth).

exercises.statement: We arrived on the seven June.
exercises.explanation: We arrived on the seventh of June. Dates need an ordinal number: the seventh, not seven.

exercises.prompt: My birthday is the ___ of August.
exercises.explanation: 31 as a date is the thirty-first.

exercises.prompt: The ___ were in favour of the new airport; about 80%, I think.
exercises.explanation: More than 50% of a group is the majority.

exercises.prompt: A small ___ did not support the idea, but it was only 5%.
exercises.explanation: Less than 50% of a group is the minority.

exercises.prompt: When I tried to add ___ all the numbers, I couldn't work it out.
exercises.explanation: Add up = put numbers together to reach a total.

exercises.prompt: Work out each calculation and match it with the answer in words.

exercises.answer: nine four oh, double three eight
exercises.explanation: In phone numbers we say oh (or zero) for 0, and double for two identical figures.
